radiusSource: 0.116795376 solar radii, the planet radius in Lally et al. (2025)'s deposited ThERESA configuration (Table 1: 0.11680 +/- 0.00014, from Agol et al. 2010), at 695,700 km per solar radius: 81,255 km, 1.14 Jupiter radii at 71,492 km.
orbitalPeriodSource: Lally et al. (2025) deposited configuration, porb 2.21857567 d (Table 1: 2.218575, from Agol et al. 2010).
semiMajorAxisSource: Lally et al. (2025) deposited configuration, a = 0.030994811518716577 au: 4,636,758 km, 8.863 radii of their 0.752 solar-radius star.

temperature.source: Computed here from the deposited best-fit temperature map (tmap in output_E.npy, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15103479, a 12 x 24 grid of 15 degree cells): the hottest cell and the area-weighted mean of the hemisphere centred on longitude 0. The visible longitudes follow ThERESA's rule from the times saved in the same file. The paper reports the hot spot 33.0 +0.7/-0.9 degrees east; a 3-component model it does not prefer places it 6.1 +/- 1.6 degrees from the equator.
